diagnostics.text: The AI Equity Index rose materially to 38.2, while the median one-year return climbed to 13.8% and the equal-weight return edged up to 21.3%. Average sector trading pressure slipped slightly to 47.9, so the stronger trailing performance has not coincided with more intense trading pressure. Investor’s Business Daily reported that an Nvidia partner rallied after strong earnings and guidance; Reuters separately described Anthropic’s rapid sales growth and steep losses as a test for its IPO. The contrast illustrates why strong demand for AI exposure can coexist with sharply different underlying economics.

diagnostics.message: Semicolon present; review for clause stacking.
diagnostics.text: The Chicago Fed NFCI stands at -0.49 after rising 0.04 over three months. Lender strain increased slightly to 17.4, and corporate bond-market distress edged up to 0.25. These measures point in the same direction at the margin, but not with the same intensity. The Financial Times reported a surge in default-insurance trading tied to AI debt concerns, while Morningstar reported a $40 billion GPU leasing deal involving SpaceX and private-credit firms. The reports show that very large AI-related financing and greater trading in credit protection can occur at the same time; they do not establish broad credit deterioration by themselves.
